result.topic_en: A list of research problems and plans: shortening Kummer's proof in cyclotomic fields, extending the Pascal hexagon's notable points, Euler's Diophantine problem, division of the lemniscate arc into a+ib parts, transferring Staude's string construction of the ellipsoid, and treating the fields √(a+bi) and ∛α to derive reciprocity laws.

da im Kreistheilungskörper bekannt-
lich die Idealtheorie auf die Theorie der höheren Congruenz
sich allein stützen lässt
items.english: since in the cyclotomic field, as is well known, ideal theory can be based solely on the theory of higher congruences

items.quote:
Suche nun aber den Beweis
von Kummer abzukürzen, indem nur das beim Beweise
des Fermatschen Satzes Wesentliche benutzt wird.
items.english: But now try to shorten Kummer's proof by using only what is essential for the proof of Fermat's theorem.

sche Punkte, ins unendliche fortzusetzen
items.english: Can the series of notable points of the Pascal hexagon (Pascal, Steiner, Kirkman points) be continued to infinity?

items.english: Euler's Diophantine problem. See Legendre, Number Theory, p. 140, vol. 2.

items.english: Geometric meaning of dividing the lemniscate arc into a+ib equal parts, and the geometric construction of it, if this is possible; compare Jacobi vol. 6 p. 276.

items.quote:
Die Staudesche Fadenconstruction des Ellipsoides
übertrage in die Kugel u. Liniengeometrie und siehe zu
was dort in 4 oder 5 Dimensionen dem Staudeschen
3 dimensionalen Satze über confocale Flächen
2ter Ordnung entspricht.
items.english: Transfer Staude's string construction of the ellipsoid into sphere and line geometry, and see what there, in 4 or 5 dimensions, corresponds to Staude's 3-dimensional theorem on confocal surfaces of second order.

items.english: Treat the field √(a+bi), where a and b are rational integers, in the same way as I treated the Dirichlet field, and in doing so derive the biquadratic reciprocity law; likewise the field ∛α, where α is a number of the field composed of cube roots of unity, etc.
